entities.label: Text
entities.summary: The Constitution of Apatzingán, formally the Constitutional Decree for the Liberty of Mexican America, was promulgated on 22 October 1814 by the Congress of Anahuac gathered in the city of Apatzingán because of the persecution of the troops of Félix María Calleja. The constitution was valid for insurgent forces in the territories that it controlled during the Mexican War of Independence.
